title: Determination of Microplastic Concentration by Micro-Raman Spectroscopy
author: Yang, Arakawa

steps.title: Prepare standard SMP samples
steps.instruction: Dispense polyethylene (PE) particles (90–106 µm, Cospheric Inc.) into distilled water to make the following concentrations: 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0, 5.5, and 6.0 mg in 6.37 mL DI water in a 10 mL beaker (AS ONE Corp., Japan), yielding 0–0.94 mg mL⁻¹. Transfer each PE suspension into the Raman micro‑spectrophotometer chamber (NRS‑4500, JASCO Inc.).

steps.title: Weigh and transfer SMP sample
steps.instruction: Measure the desired amount of SMP particles on a balance with 0.1 mg readability using weighing paper. Carefully pour the particles into a beaker, rinsing the paper with distilled water. Add a magnetic stir bar, then add DI water until the water surface reaches the 6.37 mL marker (selected to fit the Raman chamber height). Place the beaker on the stage plate and cover it with a Petri dish to avoid contamination.

steps.title: Install beaker in Raman spectrometer
steps.instruction: Launch the Raman software and power the stirrer. Position the stirrer on the stage inside the spectrometer, with its control panel facing right. Align the stirrer’s center directly under the lens sight area. Place the aluminum plate (holding the beaker) onto the stirrer and adjust so that: (1) the rubber band, Point A, and Point B match the layout in Fig. 2 with the rubber‑band side facing the chamber interior; (2) the beaker is adjacent to constraints A and B; (3) the plate is rotated counter‑clockwise until constrained by the beaker limits. Verify that a 5 × objective is selected. Turn on the stirrer, set mixing speed to Speed II (fast mode), and confirm no collision noise between stir bar and beaker wall.

steps.title: Locate measurement points
steps.instruction: Using the microscope stage, move until Point A is under the lens, then manually locate its centre and record coordinates (X_A, Y_A). Trace upward‑right to Point B, locate its centre and record (X_B, Y_B). Run the provided Matlab script (https://github.com/River20104047/Beaker_Method) with [X_A,Y_A; X_B,Y_B] to compute the plate centre (C_o) and beaker centre (C_0) coordinates ([X^o,Y^o]; [X^0,Y^0]). Check the generated Matlab figure to confirm C_o lies between Point B and C_0. Move the lens to the estimated C_0 position, set stirrer speed to Speed I (slow mode), close the Raman chamber door, and fine‑tune the lens so its centre aligns with the whirlpool centre; record the coordinates (X_0, Y_0). Open the chamber, switch off the stirrer, close the chamber, and adjust the z‑axis to focus on the water surface; record the Z‑coordinate (Z_0). Re‑open the chamber, power the stirrer back on, and keep Speed I.

steps.title: Configure Raman and acquire spectra
steps.instruction: Select the 5 × objective, set exposure time to 0.1 s, and use 2 accumulations. Choose interval analysis, set a 10 × 8000 µm slit, schedule 1000 spectra per measurement with a 0.001 s interval between spectra. Using the Excel coordinate calculator (https://github.com/River20104047/Beaker_Method), input the three sampling points: C_0 = (X_0,Y_0,Z_0), C_1 = (X_1,Y_1,Z_1), C_2 = (X_2,Y_2,Z_2) (coordinates derived from the Matlab geometry). Perform three consecutive measurements at each point (total nine measurements), which takes ≈45 min (≈5 min per measurement).

steps.title: Save and export measurement data
steps.instruction: After completing all nine measurements, inspect the water surface for any particle clumps and note their presence. Save the data within the Raman software and export each of the nine measurement files as CSV files for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Analyze Raman spectra
steps.instruction: For each of the nine measurements, compute the average spectrum: \(\bar y_{C_j-m}=\frac{1}{1000}\sum_{i=1}^{1000} y_{C_j-m,i}\) where j = 0,1,2 and m = 1,2,3. Smooth each average spectrum with an 11‑point moving average. Perform baseline correction using a moving‑window method to obtain baseline‑corrected spectra \(\bar y^{b}_{C_j-m,s}=\bar y_{C_j-m,s}-\hat y^{b}_s\). Calculate the correlation coefficient R_b between each baseline‑corrected spectrum and a standard PE spectrum: \(R_{b|C_j-m}=\frac{\sum (x_s-\bar x)(\bar y^{b}_{C_j-m,s}-\bar{\bar y}^{b}_{C_j-m})}{\sqrt{\sum (x_s-\bar x)^2}\sqrt{\sum (\bar y^{b}_{C_j-m,s}-\bar{\bar y}^{b}_{C_j-m})^2}}\). Fit the modified Langmuir model \(R_b = \frac{b_1 b_2 C_{PE}}{b_2 C_{PE}+1}+c\) (where b_1, b_2, b_3 are Langmuir parameters and c corrects for potential negative R_b) to relate R_b to PE concentration.

steps.title: Acquire Raman spectra at three points (reference)
steps.instruction: Collect Raman spectra on the water surface at three locations: centre of beaker (C_0), 1 mm from centre (C_1), and 2 mm from centre (C_2) using a 5 × objective. At each point acquire three sets of 1000 spectra (400–4000 cm⁻¹) with 0.1 s exposure, 532 nm excitation laser, 41.4 W laser power, 10 × 8000 µm slit, and 2 accumulations. Also acquire a standard PE spectrum (2 s exposure) under identical settings for reference.
